assessments.reasoning: Printed p. 383 defines JOB as the start of a job, the preceding job's end when jobs are stacked, and a JOB name beginning in column 3. The syntax box requires a JOB statement per complete job.

challenge.method: Check complete job versus procedure or original submission text. Read the started-task note, chapter 7's procedure route, and IBM's documented TSO SUBMIT generation case. Compare the null statement described on p. 2.
challenge.results: The first JOB statement is the frame for a job and a later JOB can close a preceding one in a stacked stream. A reusable procedure or the input to TSO SUBMIT can lack a source-written JOB statement. A null statement is another job boundary.

limitations: The claim describes JOB framing and name position in the February issue. Its scope leaves generated statements, started tasks, installation accounting requirements, and duplicate names separate.
